# Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite

## Goal

Add the failing-first regression tests for the stale-branch half of
SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G (AC3/AC4) so the implementation children have a pinned
contract. The tree stays green: every new test is marked
`pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` naming
SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G while the behaviour is absent, and the implementation
children remove the markers when the behaviour lands — a `strict=True`
`xpass` is a hard failure, so a marker can never be forgotten.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command — pinned here by a regression test.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures — pinned here by a regression test over the extended contract.
- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed — pinned here by regression tests.
- Regression tests cover `git_worktree_add` / `phase_start` stale-branch handling (reuse, fast-forward, actionable error, cleanup).
- Every new test is marked `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` in this item so the suite is green on landing; the implementing children flip the markers to normal passing tests.
- Tests build their own scratch git repository under `tmp_path` (no network, no writes outside it) and assert the concrete report field they will consume (`reused_branch`, `branch_fast_forwarded`, the named-branch error text, `branch_removed` / `branch_retained`) rather than only that an exception was raised.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New test module `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` mirroring the
  module-loading fixture in `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`.
- Extend `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py` (reuse/fast-forward/actionable
  error on an existing branch) and `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
  (branch removal, and retention when the branch carries the only copy of a
  commit) where their existing harness already fits.
- Reuse `shared.git_sandbox.init_repo` / `run_git` to create the three branch
  states: identical to the parent branch, strictly behind it, and carrying a
  unique commit.
- Each test names SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G in its `xfail` reason so the marker is
  self-documenting and grep-able.

## Constraints

- Do not modify production code in this item (tests only).
- The suite must be green when this item finishes (xfail-marked tests are
  reported as xfailed, not failures).
- Use the test skill for the changed-scope gate; no ad-hoc pytest runs.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (new)

- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (read-only reference: `phase_start` step 7, `git_worktree_add`, `phase_abort`)

# Recover guarded-child delegation guard

## Goal

Restore the `do-not-delegate` guard in `implement.py` automatic parent
recursion. A complete implementation, test suite and docs edit already exist
in the recoverable commit `91c9b44d1` (from the now-deleted subset item
SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876); this child replays that work onto the current tree
rather than re-deriving it.

Provenance: `git show 91c9b44d1` — files
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` (612 lines).
Its base `c818324b1` is an ancestor of `dev`, so it replays cleanly except
for one deliberate adaptation (below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (`skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (`"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking.
- Guarded children are never started, claimed, or re-attempted by `parent`; startable siblings still proceed, and a guarded child is never advanced past (guarded is not terminal, so the parent does not complete while guarded children remain).
- Direct `implement.py start <child>` / `drive <child>` on a `do-not-delegate` child continues to work (that explicit invocation is the documented override); only automatic parent recursion is gated.
- `phase_drive` spawns no session for a guarded child and forwards `guarded_children` for parity with `phase_parent`.
- Guard precedence is adapted to the current tree: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-do-not-delegate` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`, so a `blocked` child is never masked as guarded (nor guarded as `blocked`).
- Regression tests cover `_classify_child` / `_next_child_to_implement` with `do-not-delegate` children (guarded skipped, siblings still selected, override path unaffected).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` is present and passing against the current tree, and the existing parent-recursion/dependency test suites still pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Replay the guarded-child hunks of `91c9b44d1`: `DO_NOT_DELEGATE_TAG`,
  `ACTION_SKIP_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`, `ACTION_SKIPPED_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`,
  `_has_do_not_delegate_tag()`, and the `_classify_child` branch.
- Insert the guard **before** the `blocked` branch in `_classify_child`
  (the recovered commit predates `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`); `_classify_child`
  keeps its current `(child, blockers, children)` signature.
- Port the `_next_child_to_implement` skip and the `phase_parent` child-loop
  branch (`guarded_ids`, `children_processed` entry, `guarded_children`
  report field, guarded-specific waiting message) and the `phase_drive`
  forwarding.
- Restore the recovered tests, then add one test pinning the new precedence
  (a guarded child that is also `status: blocked` classifies as guarded).
- Restore the recovered `SKILL.md` / reference-doc guard paragraphs; the docs
  child later owns the stale-branch documentation.

## Constraints

- Replay, do not blind-cherry-pick: `git show 91c9b44d1 -- <path>` is the
  source of truth; resolve the intervening changes by hand and keep the
  current file's style and docstrings.
- No behaviour change for terminal, held, in-progress, blocked or plain
  startable children.
- Idempotent: re-running `parent` on a guarded child performs no claim, no

# Implement branch-aware worktree creation

## Goal

Make `phase_start` branch-aware so an existing child branch no longer fails
generically with "Failed to create worktree". The branch is either reused
(identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch) or the operator gets
an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures (`created` / `branch-exists` / `failed` verdicts), with the single `phase_start` call site updated and the source-order assertion in `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` kept satisfied.
- Reuse path: a branch whose tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) the parent branch is fast-forwarded to the parent tip with `git branch -f` and registered with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`); the report sets `reused_branch: true` and `branch_fast_forwarded: true|false`.
- Unsafe path: a branch carrying commits not reachable from the parent branch (or from `origin/<parent_branch>`) is never reset or reused silently; `phase_start` fails with the branch name, the unique-commit count and the exact recovery commands, and resets the item to `open`.
- A branch checked out in another worktree is reported by name and never raced.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Introduce verdict constants + `branch_exists(repo_root, branch)` (via
  `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`) and
  `_branch_reuse_verdict(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `identical` / `fast-forwardable` / `unique-commits`, plus
  `_branch_checked_out_in_other_worktree(repo_root, branch)`.
- Change `git_worktree_add` to return the verdict string; keep the call
  prefix `git_worktree_add(branch,` so existing source-order assertions hold.
- In `phase_start` step 7, when `not resumed` and `branch_exists`: compute the
  verdict, fast-forward when safe, then register the worktree from the
  existing branch; otherwise set `report["success"] = False`,
  `report["stale_branch"] = {branch, unique_commits, recovery_commands}` and
  return after resetting status to `open`.
- Report the decision under `report["steps"]["worktree_branch"]` so `parent`
  and `drive` reports surface why a start reused a branch.

## Constraints

- Never `git branch -f`, `reset` or delete a branch that has commits absent
  from the parent branch — reuse is limited to branches with no unique
  commits.
- Do not weaken the main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, code
  freeze gate, or parent-tracking assertion.
- Preserve `--worktree-path` override semantics and the idempotent worktree
  resume path (`_is_worktree`).
- Re-running `start` after a successful reuse must be idempotent (no second
  branch, no second worktree, no duplicate comment).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add`, new branch helpers, `phase_start` step 7
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` (source-order assertion)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Verdict-returning `git_worktree_add` plus branch state helpers.
- `phase_start` reuse / fast-forward / actionable-error behaviour.
- Green regression tests for the AC3 matrix.

# Implement safe branch cleanup

## Goal

Stop a failed or aborted `start` from poisoning the next `start` with a
orphaned feature branch: clean up the branch this run created, remove the
abandoned branch on `abort` when it is safe to do so, and always report what
was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- The failed-`start` cleanup also removes the worktree registration it created, so no half-created `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` directory survives the failure.
- `phase_abort` discovers the abandoned branch by prefix (`refs/heads/wl-<item-id>-*`) rather than needing the item title, deletes it with `git branch -d` semantics only when it has no unique commits, and reports `branch_removed` / `branch_retained` with the reason and the recovery command.
- A branch that carries commits not reachable from the parent branch or `origin/<parent_branch>` is retained and named in the abort report and comment — never force-deleted.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New `_delete_branch_if_safe(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `{deleted, reason, unique_commits}` with reasons `deleted` / `not-found` /
  `unique-commits` / `checked-out-elsewhere` / `error`; unique-commit count is
  taken against both the local parent branch and `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- New `_discover_item_branches(repo_root, work_item_id)` via
  `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) "refs/heads/wl-<id>-*"`.
- Wrap the post-`git worktree add` steps of `phase_start` so a failure after
  creation removes the worktree (guarded by `_remove_worktree`) and then
  deletes the branch this run created, reporting
  `report["cleanup"] = {worktree_removed, branch_removed, reason}`.
- In `phase_abort`, after the worktree removal and before
  `_restore_repo_state`, delete each discovered item branch that is safe and
  record the outcome on the abort comment.

## Constraints

- No blind `git branch -D`: deletion is only reached when the unique-commit
  count is zero, and a branch checked out in another worktree is never
  touched.
- Cleanup failures are logged and reported, never fatal to `abort`.
- Idempotent: a second abort finds no branch and reports `not-found` without
  error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_delete_branch_if_safe`, `_discover_item_branches`, `phase_start` post-create failure path, `phase_abort`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite".
- Blocked by "Implement branch-aware worktree creation" (shares the branch
  helpers and must not conflict on the `phase_start` failure path).

## Deliverables

- Guarded branch deletion helper and item-branch discovery.
- Failed-start cleanup of the worktree and the branch it created.
- Abort-time branch removal/retention reporting.

# Create wrapper script and suite→source mapping

## Goal
Create the Python wrapper script (`run_mutation.py`) that:
1. Resolves the target project root (no hardcoded paths, like `test-churn`)
2. Merges the base Stryker config with project-specific overrides (mutation scope)
3. Invokes Stryker (via `npx` or a local install)
4. Parses the JSON report and extracts per-module mutation scores
5. Enforces the runtime bound and flags a budget breach with partial results

Also create `scripts/suite_source_map.json` documenting which source modules are exercised by which top-churn test suites.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The campaign runs against the source modules primarily exercised by the top three churn test suites, with a documented suite→source mapping, and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
- [ ] Runtime cost is measured and bounded (confirmed bound: ≤15 min per module, ≤45 min per scoped run, weekly or per-release) so the campaign can be run periodically; the bound and cadence are documented. If the campaign cannot produce results within the bound, the report must flag this explicitly rather than silently returning partial/no results. The periodic run is scheduled on a per-project day/time that spreads CPU load across projects.
- [ ] `skill/mutation-test/scripts/run_mutation.py` resolves the project root from `--project-root` and writes `mutation_report.json` + `mutation_testing_report.md` to `--output-dir`.
- [ ] Config merging: base Stryker config + scope overrides (mutate paths) per module; a wall-clock timer per module; budget breach emits a flag plus the partial result.

# Test-first: `start` base-ref harness and current-behaviour characterisation

Build the executable test harness for `start`'s worktree base-ref resolution
(parent item **SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK**), plus characterisation coverage of the
behaviour that must survive the fix. This item lands **green**; the new
behaviour's red-first cases are written inside the implementation child
(SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX), because a committed red tree cannot be pushed — the
`finish` changed-scope gate requires a passing suite.

## Test file

`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` (new). Reuse the hermetic
patterns already in this package: a real temporary git repo with a bare `origin`
(see `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`'s `git_repo` fixture) plus
patched-boundary helpers (see `test_phase_start_claim.py`'s `_mocked_phase_start`).

## Deliverables

1. **Diverged-base fixture**: a builder that creates a repo where `origin/dev`
   has advanced past a stale, diverged local `dev` (e.g. `ahead 1, behind 1`),
   overridable for `behind`-only, `ahead`-only, dirty-checkout and
   lock-held scenarios. Exported as a reusable helper for the implementation

# Fork the `start` worktree from `origin/<parent>` when the local parent is behind

Implement the fix specified by the parent item **SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK**, in TDD order,
on top of the harness delivered by **SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK**.

## Change

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

1. `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): on every safe-skip path where the counts are
   computable, add `ahead` / `behind` (from
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) to the
   result alongside `reason` / `warning`. Counts are best-effort: a failed `rev-list`
   leaves them absent and never fails the refresh.
2. New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
   returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`. It selects
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, covering diverged), otherwise the local `parent_branch`. It never
   updates the local ref and never force-moves anything.
3. `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): fork with the resolved ref instead of the bare
   local branch name, and record `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`.
4. `phase_start` start/resume comment (~line 11431): name the base ref used and, when
   the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
5. `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): accept/document a fully-qualified remote-tracking
   base ref, and keep the `--track` upstream behaviour (`branch.<new>.remote = origin`,
   `merge = refs/heads/<parent>`) so `finish`'s push-to-`dev` semantics are unchanged.

Preserve fail-open: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch or a dirty main checkout
must never block `start`, and a diverged local branch must never be force-updated.

## Tests (written first, inside this worktree)

Add to `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, using the fixture from
SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK. Write each case, observe it fail, record the red evidence in a
work-item comment, then implement until all pass. Tests and fix land together — never
commit a red tree (the `finish` changed-scope gate requires a passing suite).

New cases:

1. **Diverged local `dev`** (`ahead >0, behind >0`): `start` forks from
   `refs/remotes/origin/dev`; the new branch's merge-base with `origin/dev` is
   `origin/dev`'s tip; `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]` carries `ref`, `reason`,
   `ahead`, `behind`.
2. **Behind-only local `dev` with a skipped refresh** (lock held; and separately a dirty
   main checkout): still forks from `origin/dev` and `start` succeeds.
3. **Local-ahead-only `dev`** (`behind 0`): base stays the local `dev` branch.
4. **Fetch failed**: base stays the local `dev` branch, `start` succeeds, reason recorded.
5. **AC3 end-to-end**: a synthetic diverged branch where `origin/dev` carries a fix the
   stale local `dev` lacks; after `start` the new worktree's tree contains that fix, so a
   first changed-scope gate runs against the fixed source with no manual rebase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: when the local `dev` is diverged or behind, the worktree is
  forked from `refs/remotes/origin/dev` instead of the stale local ref, and the created
  branch's merge-base with `origin/dev` is `origin/dev`'s tip.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent
  branch was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind
  counts — `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]` carries `ref`, `reason`, `ahead`, `behind`,
  and the worklog start/resume comment states the same.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first
  changed-scope gate without a manual rebase: the regression test with a synthetic diverged
  local branch shows the new worktree's tree already contains the fix `origin/dev` carries.
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held, dirty-checkout or fetch-failed
  refresh still fails open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch
  (the diverged local `dev` tip is unchanged after `start`).
- **AC5** — The new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` in both base-ref paths, so
  `finish`'s push-to-`dev` path is unchanged.
- **AC6** — Red-first evidence for the new cases is recorded as a comment on this item
  before the implementation is committed, and no test is left skipped or xfail.
- **AC7** — `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` and the rest of the
  `skill/implement` changed scope pass via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`

## Impact

Child sessions start from the published base instead of a stale local `dev`, so a driven
child no longer needs a manual rebase before its first gate.

# Set assignee per skill

## Problem statement

Skills currently claim work items using the producer identity (`Map`) as the assignee. This makes an agent's claim indistinguishable from a producer hold and prevents the claim reaper from identifying which skill is actually working. Each skill should instead claim with its own name.

## Users

- **Producers** — need to identify which skill is actively working on a work item from the assignee field.
- **Automated systems** (downtime dispatcher, claim reaper) — need accurate assignee attribution to detect and release stale claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Intake skill** — `intake.py start` defaults to `assignee="Intake"` when no explicit assignee is passed; callers that hard-code `--assignee Map` are updated to either omit the flag (using the new default) or use `--assignee Intake`.
2. **Plan skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim in the plan skill's documentation is updated to `--assignee Plan` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
3. **Implement skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Implement` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
4. **Audit skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Audit` (or removed if already using `--assignee ""`).
5. **All other skill documentation** — any remaining references to `--assignee Map` in SKILL.md files are updated to use the appropriate skill name.
6. **Assignee release unchanged** — the assignee-clearing behaviour on every terminal outcome (finish, auto-complete, abort, error) is preserved exactly as-is.

## Impact

Producers and automated systems can now distinguish which skill is actively working on a work item by inspecting the assignee field, and the claim reaper can reliably identify and release stale skill-level claims.

## Constraints

- Only the *claim* assignee changes; release-by-default on every terminal outcome is unaffected.
- The `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT` constant and the `claim_release.py` shared module must continue to treat `Map` as a claimable identity — no changes to shared infrastructure.
- No new work items should be created during the change; only existing skill documentation and any skill scripts that hard-code `Map` are modified.

## Existing state

- The intake skill instructs agents to pass `--assignee Map` to `intake.py start`.
- The `claim_release.py` module defines `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"` and treats it as a normal claim (released on terminal outcomes).
- The plan skill already claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).
- The implement skill also claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).

## Desired change

Replace `--assignee Map` with the skill's own name (e.g., `--assignee Intake`, `--assignee Audit`) in skill documentation and any scripts that hard-code this pattern, so each skill's claim is self-attributing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — Update `--assignee Map` references to `--assignee Intake`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/scripts/intake.py` — Change default assignee in `cmd_start` from None to `"Intake"`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md` — Check for any `--assignee Map` references; update if present.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/claim_release.py` — No changes required (Map remains a valid claimable identity).

## Related work

- SA-0MW7QTAHW0030FGV — Planned items are still left with an assignee (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK — T1: Table-driven assignee-release regression matrix (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL — Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ — Migrate callers and pin intentional holds (completed)
- SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM — implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the task scope is clear from the work-item description.

## Context

Child of **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU** (Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects). Implements parent **AC4** (dated, idempotent scheduled output) and **AC5** (failures surfaced, never a silent success). Producer decisions Q1–Q3 are settled in the parent brief: per-project `/skill:test-churn` entries, checked-in managed-root list, 7-day default interval.

## Scope

A thin, deterministic wrapper over the existing analyser
(`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`) that a scheduled
`/skill:test-churn` run invokes, so a scheduled run cannot drift from the
documented output contract. The wrapper owns path resolution and exit-code
propagation only — all analysis stays in the analyser (no duplicate logic).

Design decisions (documented, not open questions):

- Output is pinned to `<root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md`
  and `test_churn_data.json`; `--report-name`/`--json-name` are not exposed by
  the wrapper so the scheduled contract cannot be re-pointed per call.
- **History is intentionally unbounded** by default (`--max-commits 0`). The
  analyser's growth metrics are whole-history by definition, so a default
  commit bound would silently change the trend. CPU cost is mitigated by the
  staggering and `priority: low` in the provisioning child, per the parent's
  CPU-blocking risk. `--since`/`--max-commits` remain pass-through options for
  constrained runs.
- `--date` is injectable so tests are clock-independent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run_scheduled.py --root <git repo> --date 2026-11-14` writes exactly
  `reports/test-churn/2026-11-14/test_churn_report.md` and
  `reports/test-churn/2026-11-14/test_churn_data.json` beneath the root and
  exits 0.
- Re-running the identical command on the same date overwrites those two
  files, and the recursive file/directory listing of `reports/test-churn/` is
  byte-for-byte identical before and after (no numbered duplicates, no nested
  dated directories).
- A root that is absent, is not a git work tree, or fails inside the analyser
  (`GitError`) yields a non-zero exit code and a per-root error line on
  stderr, plus a run summary; it is never reported as success.
- `--since`, `--max-commits`, `--branch` and `--quiet` are passed through to
  the analyser unchanged (covered by a test that asserts the child-process
  argv).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Scheduled runs" section covering
  enable/disable, the dated output path, failure behaviour (non-zero exit,
  stderr), the interval override, and the whole-history rationale.
- Tests exercise each bullet above and are run through `/skill:test`.

### Parent AC traceability (verbatim parent ACs delivered by this slice)

- Parent AC4: Each scheduled run writes `<project-root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and `test_churn_data.json`; a re-run on the same date deterministically overwrites those two files and creates no duplicate files or directories.
- Parent AC5: Failures are surfaced: an inaccessible, non-git, or analyser-error root produces a non-zero exit code and a per-root error line on stderr (plus a run summary), and is never reported as a silent success.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test-churn/scripts/run_scheduled.py (new)
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_scheduled_runs.py (new)
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md

## Out of scope

- Provisioning / scheduling entries (sibling child item).
- Any change to the analyser's metric definitions.

## Impact

A scheduled test-churn run can be trusted to leave a dated, self-describing report on disk and to shout when it fails, instead of silently producing nothing.

data.description:
## Context

Child of **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU**. Implements parent **AC1** (schema-valid entry), **AC2** (create-if-absent provisioning, including Tableau-Card-Engine which has no scheduled-prompts file), **AC3** (mandatory deterministic staggering — no CPU blocking), **AC6** (configurable interval, default 7 days) and the provisioning/staggering half of **AC7**.

The schedule file format is owned by the external `worklog`/herdr package
(`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`): `entries[]` of
`{id, prompt, intervalDays, lastTriggeredAt, time?, priority?}`; an absent file
is an empty set, a malformed file is an empty set (logged), and an invalid
entry is skipped. Provisioning must never rewrite or drop entries it does not
own.

## Scope

`skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py` — create-if-absent
insertion of one `/skill:test-churn` entry per managed root, with deterministic
staggering.

Documented scheme (implemented and tested here, documented in AC8 files):

- **Window:** local `02:00` + **30-minute** steps (`02:00, 02:30, …`), so eight
  roots occupy `02:00–05:30`. This deliberately avoids the `/skill:standup`
  slot at `06:05`; the parent brief's "e.g. 02:00 + 40-minute steps" is
  illustrative and a 40-minute step would put the 7th/8th slot at `06:00`/`06:40`,
  contradicting the binding "away from 06:05" constraint.
- **Day staggering:** `lastTriggeredAt = now − (index % intervalDays) days`, so
  the eight roots fall due on spread days across the 7-day cycle (the 8th root
  shares index 0's day but has a unique `time`, so no two roots are ever due in
  the same idle cycle).
- **Priority:** `priority: "low"` on the new entry, so a whole-history scan
  yields to the project's maintenance routines (schema default is `high`).
- **Idempotence:** never re-stagger or rewrite an existing
  `/skill:test-churn` entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For each managed root, provisioning inserts
  `{"id": "/skill:test-churn", "prompt": "/skill:test-churn", "intervalDays": 7,
  "time": "HH:MM", "priority": "low", "lastTriggeredAt": "<ISO-8601>"}` into
  `<root>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, creating `.worklog/` and the file
  when absent (the Tableau-Card-Engine case).
- All pre-existing entries — including their `lastTriggeredAt`, `time`,
  `priority`, unknown extra keys and schema-invalid entries — survive unchanged
  and in order, with the new entry appended; an unparseable (malformed) file is
  left untouched and reported as an error with a non-zero exit code.
- A second run reports "already present" for every root and writes nothing
  (assert unchanged bytes and mtimes); an existing entry is never re-staggered.
- Staggering is deterministic for a given `--now` and root list: every root has
  a unique `time` inside the documented window, `06:05` is never used, and the
  `lastTriggeredAt` day offsets are spread as `index % intervalDays`.
- `--dry-run` reports planned writes and performs none; `--root` (repeatable)
  overrides the checked-in list; `--interval-days` overrides the default 7 in
  both the entry and the day-offset arithmetic.
- Tests cover every bullet above (insert, preserve, idempotent re-run,
  create-if-absent, malformed config, unique times, spread offsets, dry-run,
  flags), run through `/skill:test`.

### Parent AC traceability (verbatim parent ACs delivered by this slice)

- Parent AC1: A `/skill:test-churn` entry is registered in SorraAgents' `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` using the existing schema (`id`, non-empty `prompt`, positive `intervalDays`, valid `HH:MM` `time`, and `lastTriggeredAt`), with the first provision setting a deterministic, staggered `lastTriggeredAt` seed and a distinct `time` (see AC3); re-running provisioning neither duplicates the entry, re-staggers it, nor changes any other entry's `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Parent AC3: **Staggering (no CPU blocking):** provisioned entries are spread deterministically across the managed set so no two projects are due in the same idle cycle. Each entry gets a unique `time` within a documented window (away from the 06:05 standup slot), and its `lastTriggeredAt` seed offsets its `intervalDays` cycle by a project-index-derived amount. The scheme is deterministic for a given managed-root list and clock (injectable `--now` for tests), documented, and covered by tests asserting no duplicate `time` values and evenly spread day offsets.
- Parent AC6: The interval is configurable per entry in `scheduled-prompts.json` and via a provisioning `--interval-days` flag; the default (**7 days, weekly**) is documented in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` with its rationale.
- Parent AC7: Automated tests cover: entry provisioning (insert, preserve other entries, idempotent re-run, create-if-absent including an absent file, malformed or invalid config), staggering (unique `time`, spread day offsets, no re-stagger on re-run), managed-root iteration (existing, absent and non-git roots), date-partitioned output and idempotent overwrite, and non-zero failure propagation.

**Key Files:**
- skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py (new)
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_scheduled_runs.py
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md

## Out of scope

- Executing the provisioning against sibling project roots (next child item).
- Any change to the external herdr/worklog package.

## Impact

Every managed project becomes self-registering for weekly test-health evidence, spread across the week so no two heavy scans start together.

Deliver the byte-preserving removal API and a single tolerant marker parser used by both removal and duplicate detection.

## Goal

Add `remove_refactor_marker()` plus one parser that locates every marker style without normalising the file.

## Impact

Developers and agents can delete a stale REFACTOR marker without touching surrounding code or rewriting a file's line endings.

## Context

Parent SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9. Two divergent regexes currently parse markers (`comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`); unify them so Markdown/CSS markers are not missed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- One tolerant marker parser replaces both existing regexes; `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` is rewritten in terms of it.
- File IO uses `newline=""` for read and write, so removal never normalises CRLF; optional ` * ` prefixes in CSS blocks are tolerated.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> {"removed": bool, "reason": str}` to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`.
- Add one compiled parser that locates the full block for an id across all four comment styles (line-prefixed and native block, optional ` * ` prefixes).
- Remove exactly the bytes the injector added (leading separator newline when present) and restore the trailing newline exactly.
- Add an optional `is_active: Callable[[str], bool] | None` parameter to `has_existing_comment()`; export the unified pattern for `workitem_creation`.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on "Test: REFACTOR marker removal API".

# Behavioural tests: lossless waiter relay (`JobOutputTail`)

Test-first coverage for the relay half of SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO (parent AC3, AC6).

`skill/shared/wait_for_job.py::JobOutputTail.new_lines()` currently returns
`lines[-self.tail_lines:]`, silently discarding every line above the cap in a
poll window (default `--tail-lines 10`). A poll window that catches 200 build
lines shows only 10 and says nothing about the other 190. This child adds the
failing tests that pin the required behaviour **before** the fix lands.

Reuse the existing harness in `skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py`
(tmp log files, offset semantics, rotation) — extend, do not reimplement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A test asserts that `new_lines()` on a poll window whose new-line count
   exceeds `tail_lines` does **not** silently drop lines: the returned list is
   either all new lines, or ends with an explicit omission marker matching
   `… N lines omitted` (with N equal to the number of dropped lines).
2. A test asserts losslessness (no marker) when the window holds fewer lines
   than `tail_lines` — the default must be lossless for typical poll windows.
3. A test asserts the omission marker names the exact dropped count and
   mentions `--tail-lines` as the remedy.
4. A test asserts the helper emits exactly **one** liveness/progress line per
   wait poll — no duplicate `progress:` + `heartbeat:` pair in one window.
5. A test asserts existing behaviour is unchanged: first-poll tail seeding,
   incremental offset reporting, rotation/truncation restart, empty source →
   `[]`.
6. The tests fail against the current implementation (red) and are runnable
   in isolation via the test skill's changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py` — existing harness to extend.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.

## Deliverables

# Fix JobOutputTail: lossless relay + explicit omission + single liveness line

Fix `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` so the relay never silently drops output.

Relates to SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO (parent AC3) and SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK (waiter
already streams — this item fixes the producer-side silence that makes the
drop irrelevant).

## Problem

`new_lines()` returns `lines[-self.tail_lines:]`, silently discarding lines
above the cap. A poll window catching 200 lines shows only 10 — the operator
sees a gap of silence and the agent's context budget is wasted on a truncated
tail.

## Solution

`new_lines()` now returns **all** new lines. When a burst would exceed a
reasonable bound (the caller's `--tail-lines`), the helper appends a single
omission marker: `… N lines omitted; raise --tail-lines or poll faster`
(replacing the last N entries). The caller (wait loop) still honours
`--tail-lines` for its own context budget.

The wait loop also deduplicates liveness lines: only one `progress:` or
`heartbeat:` per poll window, even if multiple heartbeat sources fire.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `new_lines()` returns all new lines when burst ≤ `tail_lines` (lossless).
2. When burst > `tail_lines`, the last entry is replaced with an omission
   marker `… N lines omitted; raise --tail-lines or poll faster` where N is
   the count of dropped lines.
3. The wait loop emits exactly one liveness/progress line per poll —
   deduplicated against the previous poll's heartbeat.
4. All existing tests pass; the tests from the sibling test item (SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO relay tests) pass.
5. The helper's CLI surface and exit codes unchanged; `--tail-lines` still
   controls the caller's context budget.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py::JobOutputTail.new_lines` — core fix.
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — wait loop liveness dedup.

## Dependencies

Sibling test item: test-first behavioural tests for lossless relay.

## Deliverables

- Fixed `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` + wait loop dedup.
- All tests green (existing + new from sibling test item).

Test-first coverage for the producer half of SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO (parent AC1, AC2, AC6).

The streaming runner forwards child subprocess output line-by-line to stderr
(with flush) **while** still capturing the full text for the step report and

3. A test verifies the runner handles both stdout and stderr from the child

   propagated correctly (the finish gate still blocks on failure).

# implement.py: tee-style streaming runner for build/tests/push

Wire implement.py's subprocess runners to stream live output to the Pi TUI.

Relates to SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO (parent AC1, AC2). The fix lives in
`implement.py` — no pi extension, no custom tool.

## Problem

`run_cmd()`, `_shell_command_runner()`, and `git_push_to_dev()` all run
subprocesses with `capture=True` / `capture_output=True` / `communicate()`.
No output reaches implement.py's stdout/stderr until the child exits, so
a 2-minute build or 40-minute test suite produces **zero** feedback in the
TUI until completion.

## Solution

Add a `_tee_runner()` function that:
- Spawns the child subprocess with `stdout=subprocess.PIPE`, `stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`
- Reads child output line-by-line in a background thread (non-blocking)
- Forwards each line to `sys.stderr` with `flush=True` (visible in TUI)
- Still collects the full text for the step report and `--json` output
- Returns a `subprocess.CompletedProcess`-compatible result (stdout, stderr, returncode)

Phase banners are printed as flush headers:
```
→ Running build (npm run build)…
→ Build output: (live lines stream here)
→ Build complete (exit code 0, 2m36s)
```

Output goes to **stderr** so `--json` on stdout stays clean (matching the
existing timing-to-stderr convention).

`run_build()`, `_shell_command_runner()`, and `git_push_to_dev()` are wired
to use the tee runner. The test-cache runner seam passes streaming through
so the finish gate's real suite output is what appears live (AC2).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_build()` streams npm build output live; phase banners appear at
   start and end.
2. `_shell_command_runner()` (test cache path) streams suite output live
   through the tee runner.
3. `git_push_to_dev()` streams push output live (less critical but included
   for completeness).
4. All streamed output goes to stderr; `--json` stdout is unchanged.
5. The step report still contains the full captured output (for `--json`).
6. Tests from the sibling test item (SA-0MVIQ8A5H008T5ZO runner tests) pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add `_tee_runner()`, wire into
  `run_build()`, `_shell_command_runner()`, `git_push_to_dev()`.

## Dependencies

Sibling test item: test-first behavioural tests for streaming runner.

## Deliverables

- `_tee_runner()` in `implement.py`.
- `run_build()`, `_shell_command_runner()`, `git_push_to_dev()` wired.
- All tests green.

## Goal

Add the core classification function that determines whether a work item was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker or manually dispatched by the operator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: classify_auto_dispatch(item_id, window_start, window_end, worklog_dir) returns True if any of these conditions hold:
  (a) A matching entry in .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log where itemId == item_id and outcome != spawn-failed (ignore outcome field if absent — pre-enrichment entries are still valid).
  (b) A worklog comment on the item containing the prefix Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at.
  (c) A matching entry in downtime-dispatches.log with kind: scheduled (scheduled prompts count as auto-dispatch).

- [ ] AC2: Returns False (manual) for:
  (a) outcome: spawn-failed entries — not a successful dispatch.
  (b) Items found only in downtime-coordination.log or local-route.log — must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
  (c) Items with no matching dispatch log entry AND no comment marker.

- [ ] AC3: Read-side failures degrade gracefully — missing/unreadable .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log file, unparseable JSONL lines, or wl comment list failure causes the function to log a warning (stderr) and fall through to the manual bucket for that item. The function never raises.

- [ ] AC4: The dispatch log lookup uses the worklog_dir to locate the file (respects --worklog-dir / WL_WORKLOG_DIR); when no worklog_dir is set, falls back to cwd/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log.

- [ ] AC5: Unit-tested with fixtures: (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) outcome: spawn-failed entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in downtime-coordination.log / local-route.log only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

## Goal

As a maintainer of this repository, I want a committed, reproducible baseline of
what the test suite costs and how it has grown, so that every later prune/rework
decision in the epic is provable against numbers rather than intuition.

## Context

Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` (AC1, AC7) needs the measurement half of the
test-value pipeline. The epic already quotes test-churn-analyser v2.1.0 numbers
from `dev` @ `7875214`; this item refreshes them at the refactor's baseline
commit and adds the runtime and inventory dimensions the analyser does not
produce.

In-scope inventory measured at planning time (tracked files only):
431 test files — 375 pytest (`test_*.py`) and 56 node (`*.test.mjs` /
`test-*.mjs`). Per-area: `tests/` 176, `skill/audit` 64, `skill/implement` 51,
`skill/shared` 30, `skill/test` 15, `skill/standup` 12, `skill/machine-hygiene`
7, `skill/intake` 5, remaining skills ≤3 each, `command/` 1.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/test-value-baseline.md` — human-readable baseline: definitions, the
  exact commands used, the numbers, and the caveats.
- `docs/dev/test-value-baseline.json` — machine-readable mirror of the same
  numbers (consumed by the Classify and Report children).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Enumerate the in-scope set from tracked files only:
   `git ls-files` filtered to `test_*.py`, `*.test.{mjs,js,ts}` and
   `test-*.mjs`; **exclude `.worklog/worktrees/**`** (untracked copies of the
   whole repo — 7k+ phantom test files), helpers, fixtures and setup files.
   Record the count and per-area breakdown.
2. Refresh the churn baseline with
   `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` at the baseline commit;
   record both rewrite-ratio variants with their denominators, test files/lines
   added vs deleted, net growth, and the per-quarter trend.
3. Capture suite wall-clock runtime through the test skill only
   (`run_tests.py --suite all --type full --json`, `elapsed_seconds`), once per
   suite (pytest, node) and at least twice, recording the median and the host /
   parallelism caveat. Never invoke `pytest`/`node --test` directly.
4. Capture per-file runtime if the runner already exposes it; if it does not,
   record that limitation and cross-reference `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` (per-test
   runtime and flakiness) rather than building a second measurement path.
5. Commit both artefacts and cite the baseline commit + analyser version.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-value-baseline.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-baseline.json`
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A baseline is recorded in this item and committed under `docs/dev/`: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, the in-scope test-file inventory, and a cross-link to the per-file verdicts produced by the Classify child — together satisfying the epic's AC1.
- [ ] Both rewrite-ratio variants are recorded with their denominators, alongside the analyser version and the baseline commit, and net file/line growth plus the per-quarter trend are recorded.
- [ ] Suite wall-clock runtime is recorded per suite (pytest, node) as the median of at least two runs taken through the test skill, with the timing caveat (host, parallelism) documented.
- [ ] The in-scope inventory enumerates tracked test files only, states the total and the per-area breakdown, and explicitly excludes `.worklog/worktrees/**`, helpers, fixtures and setup files.
- [ ] Every recorded number is reproducible from a command written in the artefact, and the JSON mirror parses and matches the markdown figures.

## Constraints & assumptions

- Read-only against the repository's behaviour: this item must not change any
  test or production code.
- Bounded fan-out and cache-friendly: run the suite via the test skill, never
  ad-hoc suites (test execution policy).
- Assumption: per-file runtime may be unavailable without the runner work
  tracked in `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ`; recording the limitation is an acceptable
  outcome, inventing a parallel measurement is not.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC1, AC7).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: consumes this baseline for per-file verdicts.
- `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` — per-test runtime/flakiness (coordinate, do not duplicate).
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled churn runs.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict, with
evidence, for **every** test file in the suite, so that remediation is a
bounded, auditable list rather than ad-hoc inspection.

## Context

`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` already detects the four anti-pattern
classes from `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`, but it evaluates one file
per invocation. A planning-time probe over the 431 tracked test files returned
376 `keep` and 55 `remove` — enough to prove the scope is real and bounded, not
the committed baseline for this item (the probe must be re-run and recorded).

The evaluator's verdicts are **file-scoped and coarse**: a file with one
source-grep test case is reported `remove` even when the rest is sound. The
per-file verdict recorded here is therefore the agent's adjudicated verdict
(evaluator machine verdict + anti-pattern checklist + churn evidence), and a
`remove` verdict on a file is not authority to delete the file.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.md` — per-area tables of file → verdict →
  evidence reference.
- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.json` — the same, machine-readable, one
  record per in-scope file with `{file, area, verdict, reasons[]}`.
- A bounded batch mode in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a deterministic batch mode to `evaluate_usefulness.py` (for example
   `--file-list <path>` and/or `--root <dir>` with `--json`), producing a stable
   sorted list of verdict records in one process. Keep the existing single-file
   CLI and its output shape unchanged.
2. Run it across the in-scope set from the Measure baseline and record the raw
   machine verdicts in the JSON artefact.
3. Adjudicate every non-`keep` machine verdict against the anti-pattern
   checklist plus churn evidence into `keep`, `rework` or `prune`, recording the
   justification for each. Guidance:
   - placeholder / zero-assertion / self-referential simulation → `prune`
     (if nothing observable is pinned) or `rework` (if a real behaviour is
     reachable from the same file);
   - source-grep test cases → `rework` when the behaviour is observable, `prune`
     when the code/markdown it asserts no longer exists — final call belongs to
     the Prove child;
   - files whose only defect is non-hermetic real `git` → `keep`, cross-referenced
     to `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`;
   - uncertain cases → `keep`, with a discovered-from work item if a follow-up is
     genuinely needed.
4. Tag every in-scope file that touches a `.md` path with its file-usage class
   from the closed taxonomy decided on the epic — **A** sandbox fixture (`.md` is
   incidental content in a temp repo), **B** production output (production code
   writes the markdown, the test asserts the artefact), **C** link/structure
   hygiene, **D** doc-contract prose, **E** duplicate convention grep. Only class
   D/E files are rework or prune candidates; a class A/B/C file is `keep` even
   when a naive "reads a markdown file" rule would flag it. Reference counts from
   the planning pass: ≈104 files are class A, ≈22 class B, ≈9 class C, ≈22 class D,
   and the narrow per-skill convention greps are class E.
5. Reconcile the totals: verdict counts must sum exactly to the in-scope file
   count, and the artefacts record the in-scope count they reconcile against.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`
- `tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.json`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] The verdicts are produced by one deterministic batch invocation of `evaluate_usefulness.py`, whose committed JSON output is the machine input to the adjudicated verdicts — no hand-assembled per-file list.
- [ ] The batch mode is covered by tests (single file, multi-file list, zero results, mixed verdicts, deterministic ordering) and existing single-file behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Every `prune` verdict cites at least one anti-pattern class from `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` and points at the evidence entry the Prove child must fill in; files whose only defect is non-hermetic git are classified `keep` and cross-referenced to `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`.
- [ ] Every in-scope file that touches a `.md` path carries a file-usage class tag (A–E), and no class A, B or C file is given a `rework` or `prune` verdict on the strength of reading a markdown file alone.

## Constraints & assumptions

- The evaluator is a heuristic gate, not an oracle: agent adjudication is
  required and every deviation from the machine verdict is recorded with a
  reason.
- Assumption: classification runs in one static pass (no test execution), so it
  is cheap and re-runnable; it does not replace the Prove child's evidence.
- Excluded from scope: `.worklog/worktrees/**`, helpers, fixtures, setup files,
  and `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` (owned by `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23`).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC1, AC2).
- `SA-0MWG509GZ002JIBB` — Measure: supplies the in-scope inventory and churn data (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG5115X005MEIM` — Prove: turns `prune` verdicts into evidence.
- `SA-0MVXVBZT7003VOCO` — future test-value aggregator; this item must not build it, and should reuse its evaluator rather than reimplement it if it lands first.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want written evidence for every prune candidate, so that no
test is ever deleted on suspicion alone.

## Context

The epic's risk model is asymmetric: removing a useful test is a regression,
keeping a dead one only costs runtime. `prune` verdicts come from a static
heuristic (`evaluate_usefulness.py`) plus checklist adjudication; this item
converts each into proof.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/test-value-evidence.md` — one section per prune candidate:
  candidate file, the behaviours it pinned, the evidence gathered, the decision.
- The corresponding `evidence` field populated in
  `docs/dev/test-value-classification.json`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Take the `prune` set from the Classify child and, per candidate, capture:
   - `git log --follow`/`git blame` on the test and on the module or document it
     targets, recording the last meaningful change and any rename;
   - whether the targeted module/document still exists and is publicly exported;
   - a repository-wide search for the same behaviour covered through a public
     API elsewhere, recording the covering test's path and test name.
2. Classify each candidate with exactly one outcome:
   - **REMOVE** — the pinned behaviour is not observable, is gone, or is
     provably duplicated elsewhere (naming the covering test);
   - **KEEP-DESPITE-FLAG** — the evaluator/checklist is wrong; record why, and
     note whether a detector fix (with a regression test) is required.
3. Use mutation testing (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`) only as the tie-breaker where
   provenance is genuinely unclear, and record the score used.
4. Reconcile 1:1 with the Classify verdicts: every `prune` candidate has an entry
   and no entry exists for a non-candidate.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-value-evidence.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.json`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] Each evidence entry names the candidate file, the behaviour it pinned, the covering test (or an explicit "not observable" / "target module gone"), and the command whose output supports the conclusion.
- [ ] Where provenance is unclear the candidate is resolved by a recorded mutation score, or demoted to `keep` / `rework` with the conservative default stated — the tie-breaker never defaults to removal.
- [ ] The evidence set reconciles one-to-one with the `prune` verdicts: every candidate has an entry, no entry exists for a non-candidate, and candidates resolved as REMOVE are the only ones the prune child may delete.

## Constraints & assumptions

- Read-only analysis: no test or production code changes in this item.
- Evidence gathering is bounded per candidate (a handful of git/grep commands);
  mutation testing is a tie-breaker, not a default, because it is expensive.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC3).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: source of the prune candidate set (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG51CGK004RNOK` — prune remediation: consumes this evidence.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (tie-breaker).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want every proven-dead test removed, so the suite stops
paying runtime for assertions that cannot fail for a reason anyone cares about.

## Context

Deletion is the only irreversible step in this epic, so this child acts **only**
on candidates that the Prove child resolved as REMOVE. The planning-time probe
found 55 of 431 tracked test files flagged by `evaluate_usefulness.py`; the
actual delete list is expected to be far smaller because most flagged files are
partially sound and become `rework` instead.

## Deliverables

- Deleted test files (or deleted test cases within surviving files) for every
  REMOVE-verdict candidate.
- A per-batch completion comment on this item recording file → evidence entry →
  suite result.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Work from `docs/dev/test-value-evidence.md`. If nothing is resolved REMOVE,
   close this item as "no-op: no candidate with proven-dead behaviour" with the
   evidence link — that is a successful outcome, not a failure.
2. Delete whole test files where the entire file is dead/duplicate; delete the
   offending test cases (not the file) where only part of a file is dead.

   child work item per batch as soon as the delete list exceeds ~25 files, so no

4. After each batch: run the suite through the test skill (changed scope for the

5. Exclude anything owned by `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23`
   (`tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`) and anything the hermeticity item

data.description:
## Goal

As a maintainer, I want every rework-verdict test converted into a real
observable-behaviour assertion, so the suite keeps its coverage while losing its
dead weight.

## Context

This is the largest child in the epic. The planning-time probe flagged 55 of 431
tracked test files; the dominant class is source-grep (a test reads a source or
markdown file and asserts on its text), followed by placeholder/zero-assertion and
self-referential simulation cases.

**Decided** (producer delegated, recorded on `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`): this
repository deliberately carries tests that read files — 181 tracked test files
reference a `.md` path, ~127 read one. They are **not** one class, so "reads a
markdown file" is not a defect. Every in-scope file that touches `.md` is tagged
with one of five classes, and only the last two are rework/prune candidates:

| Class | What it is | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **A — sandbox fixture** | the test creates/edits `README.md`, `notes.md` etc. inside a temp repo to exercise production code | out of scope; `.md` is incidental (≈104 files) |
| **B — production output** | production code writes the `.md` (changelog, audit report, standup, churn report) and the test asserts the artefact | out of scope; keep (≈22 files) |
| **C — link/structure hygiene** | parses markdown to assert links resolve, referenced paths exist, required headings are present | keep; must parse structure, never match prose |
| **D — doc-contract** | asserts a document *states* a rule or invariant (e.g. the finish-gate semantics in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) | **rework** to parsed structure |
| **E — duplicate convention grep** | a narrow per-skill text grep whose convention is already covered generically (e.g. `tests/unit/test-triage-skill.mjs` vs `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py`) | **prune** |

Class D rule: assert parsed structure (headings, frontmatter keys, labelled
bullets, table cells, parsed links) or, where the exact wording *is* the
contract — a sentence an agent is told to quote — cite in a comment the work item
that mandates that wording. Class D must not assert raw prose substrings.

## Deliverables

- Reworked test files/cases (behaviour assertions in place of text/structural
  assertions).
- Detector corrections in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` where the
  evaluator is demonstrably wrong about a sound test, each with a regression test.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Work the `rework` verdict set from the Classify child, batched by area
   (`tests/`, `skill/audit`, `skill/implement`, `skill/shared`, `skill/test`,
   `skill/standup`, node `.mjs`), one child work item per area batch once the
   list exceeds ~25 files.
2. For each reworked case: identify the observable behaviour the source text was
   standing in for (emitted event, returned value, state transition, CLI exit
   code, rendered node, parsed document structure) and assert **that**; write the
   failing assertion first where the behaviour is already implemented so the test
   is proven able to fail.
3. Where the behaviour is genuinely unobservable, hand the case back to `prune`
   (with an evidence note) rather than inventing an assertion.
4. Where the evaluator is a false positive, fix the detector (keeping it
   conservative) and add a regression test in
   `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`; never delete a sound test to
   silence the tool.
5. Re-run `evaluate_usefulness.py` over the touched area after each batch and
   record the `remove`-count drop.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `tests/**/test_*.py`, `skill/*/tests/test_*.py`, `tests/unit/*.mjs` (targets)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text in class D (doc-contract prose) or class E (duplicate convention grep); classes A (sandbox fixture), B (production output) and C (link/structure hygiene) are explicitly exempt.
- [ ] Every in-scope file that touches a `.md` path is tagged with its file-usage class (A–E) in the classification artefact, and only class D and E files are reworked or pruned — no class A, B or C file is modified by this item.
- [ ] Class D files assert parsed structure, or cite the work-item id that mandates the exact wording when the wording itself is the contract.
- [ ] After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] Every reworked case is demonstrably able to fail: the behaviour-asserting test was observed red against a deliberately broken/mutated behaviour (or written assertion-first) before landing.
- [ ] Evaluator false positives are fixed in the detector with a regression test rather than by deleting or weakening a sound test, and each fix is recorded in the completion comment.
- [ ] Work is split into area batches when the list exceeds ~25 files, each batch green (changed scope during work, full scope before the item closes) and each batch's completion comment recording the `remove`-count drop.

## Constraints & assumptions

- No coverage-maximisation: a reworked test that asserts less but observes real
  behaviour is a success; a reworked test that asserts more text is not.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` when choosing the replacement
  assertion.
- Decision (recorded on the epic): repository-contract/inventory tests survive in
  parsed-structure form rather than being deleted wholesale; the five-class
  taxonomy above is closed for this pass, and a sixth class discovered mid-work
  is added to `test-writing-guidelines.md` with an example rather than handled
  ad hoc.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC4, AC5).
- `SA-0MWG5115X005MEIM` — Prove (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG51CGK004RNOK` — prune remediation (complementary).
- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — the 5 known source-grep tests (separate item; exclude).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer behaviour over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.

data.description:
## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the suite itself to reject a new anti-pattern test, so the
pruned classes cannot silently return.

## Context

`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` already classifies a test file as
`remove` when it finds a source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential
or duplicate-coverage pattern. What is missing is a **standing gate**: nothing runs
the evaluator over the suite, so nothing stops a new offender being added. This
child adds that gate — as a test, in test-first style, and without itself becoming
the anti-pattern it screens for.

## Deliverables

- A suite-level guard test that fails when an in-scope test file is dirty, built on
  the shared evaluator API rather than duplicated regexes.
- A documented, work-item-required exemption mechanism that must be empty at
  completion of this epic.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the guard as a test (for example `tests/test_test_value_guard.py`) that
   enumerates in-scope test files exactly as the Measure baseline does (tracked
   files only; `.worklog/worktrees/**` excluded) and calls
   `evaluate_usefulness.evaluate_file` on each, failing with a per-file report
   when any verdict is `remove` or the file contains a placeholder/zero-assertion
   case.
2. Feed the guard two fixture sets so it is proven able to fail: a clean fixture
   (passes) and an offender fixture (fails with a useful message). Do not assert on
   the guard's own source text.
3. Add a bounded, class-aware exemption mechanism: a checked-in list of
   `{path, class, work-item-id}` entries that suppresses a specific file, where
   `class` is one of the file-usage classes decided on the epic (A sandbox
   fixture, B production output, C link/structure hygiene). The list must be
   empty when this epic closes; a class D or E file may never be exempted. A test
   asserts every exemption cites a live work item and a valid class.
4. Wire the guard into the existing suite (no new runner, no new skill) and
   measure its overhead; document it in `skill/test/SKILL.md`.
5. Keep the run bounded: the static scan of ~430 files is expected to stay well
   under five seconds; if it does not, cache the verdicts by file content hash.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_test_value_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `.pi/test-config.json` (only if a group wiring change is needed)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] The guard is built on the shared evaluator API (single source of truth for the anti-pattern rules) and is proven able to fail by clean/offender fixtures.
- [ ] Every exemption to the guard cites a work item id and a file-usage class (A/B/C) in a checked-in list that is tested to reference live items; class D and E files can never be exempted, and the list is empty when the epic closes.
- [ ] The guard does not flag the ≈104 class A fixture tests or the ≈22 class B production-output tests that read or write markdown, demonstrated by fixtures for each class.
- [ ] The guard adds no new runner or skill, is documented in `skill/test/SKILL.md`, and its measured overhead is recorded (target: under five seconds on the current in-scope set).

## Constraints & assumptions

- Test-first: the guard's offender fixture must be shown red before the guard is
  accepted green.
- The guard scans **test files**, not production source: asserting on the guard's own
  or production source text would violate the very rule it enforces.
- Scope set is derived, never hardcoded per area, so new test directories are
  covered automatically.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC8).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: the anti-pattern set the guard enforces (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG51CGK004RNOK`, `SA-0MWG51S1D0084L0H` — remediation, so the guard lands on a clean suite.
- `SA-0MWG52KSC008DFKC` — documentation learnings.

data.description:
## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the pruning workflow and anti-pattern guidance to carry
what this pass learned, so the next suite-wide review starts from better criteria.

## Context

The workflow lives in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` (pruning review workflow) and the
anti-pattern catalogue in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (7 classes:
source-grep, placeholder, self-referential simulation, duplicate coverage,
type-level/structural-only, zero-assertion browser/scene, real-git without sandbox).
This pass is expected to surface at least two new refinements:

1. **File-level false positives** — the evaluator returns `remove` for a file with
   one offending case, so a verdict is never authority to delete a file.
2. **File-reading tests are not one class** — 181 tracked test files reference a
   `.md` path and ~127 read one, but only two of the five classes are defects. The
   guidelines must publish the closed taxonomy (A sandbox fixture, B production
   output, C link/structure hygiene, D doc-contract, E duplicate convention grep)
   with a real example per class, so "reads a markdown file" is never treated as a
   defect on its own.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: new/refined anti-pattern
  classes, each with a real example from this pass, the fix applied, and the
  exemption rule.
- Updated `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` pruning workflow: the measure → classify →
  prove → remediate → guard loop as executed here, with the evidence bar for a
  deletion.
- Updated `skill/test/SKILL.md` covering the evaluator batch mode and the guard.

## Minimal Implementation

1. After remediation and the guard land, replay the pass's findings against the
   two documents and add the refinements (with repo examples and file pointers).
2. State the deletion evidence bar explicitly: no removal without an evidence
   entry resolving the candidate REMOVE.
3. Document the exemption class and how a new exemption is added (work item id
   required) so the guard and the guidance cannot drift apart.
4. Keep the prose UK English and preserve existing headings/anchors that other
   tests or skills link to.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md`
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] Each new or refined class carries a real example from this repository, the fix applied, and the evidence bar for deletion — not generic advice.
- [ ] `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` publishes the closed five-class file-usage taxonomy (A fixture, B production output, C link/structure hygiene, D doc-contract, E duplicate convention grep) with one real example per class, and states the class D rule (parsed structure, or a work-item citation when the exact wording is the contract).
- [ ] `skill/test/SKILL.md` documents the evaluator's batch mode and the regression guard, cross-linking both documents and the guard's class-aware exemption rule.
- [ ] UK English throughout, existing links/anchors preserved, and the repository's documentation/link tests pass.

## Constraints & assumptions

- Documentation-only change: no behaviour change to any skill.
- The guidance must remain conservative: an ambiguous case stays `keep` and is
  filed as a work item, never silently reclassified as removable.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC9).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: source of the anti-pattern adjudications.
- `SA-0MWG5284K004J1YN` — the guard whose exemption rule this documents.
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — churn metrics in the refactor skill.

## Goal

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual, each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly): "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself".

Integrate the test-churn analyser into the refactor pipeline as an additional, non-fatal stage after smell detection, for both full-project and session-boundary modes, surfaced in the human report and `--json` output, with a `--no-churn` escape hatch and runtime (subprocess) resolution of the analyser.

## Goal

Update `select_group_from_changed_files` to return `frozenset[str] | None` instead of `str | None`, representing the union of **all** groups whose `paths` match at least one changed file. The iteration order must be deterministic (sorted group names).

## Problem

Currently `select_group_from_changed_files` returns a single group via `min()` — when multiple groups match a changed file, only one is returned. This causes the changed-scope gate to skip testing all other affected skill suites (SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9).

## Requirements

- Return `frozenset[str] | None` (sorted group names in the frozenset for determinism).
- All groups whose `paths` spec matches **any** changed file are included.
- Single-group match returns a frozenset with one element (backwards-compatible with callers that check `bool(result)`).
- `None` when no groups match (unchanged fallback).
- Deterministic: iteration order is sorted group names, not set-iteration order.
- `full` group is still intentionally excluded from selection.

## Impact

A cross-skill change set (e.g. touching implement + test + audit skills) now surfaces all affected groups, enabling the changed-scope gate to test every one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Changes to `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**`, and `skill/audit/**` returns `frozenset({"implement", "test", "audit"})`.
- AC2: A single-group change returns `frozenset({"audit"})` (single element).
- AC3: No matching files returns `None` (unchanged fallback).
- AC4: `full` group is never included in the returned frozenset.
- AC5: Existing single-match tests in `TestChangedFileToGroup` are updated to expect frozenset returns.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `select_group_from_changed_files` (line ~1614)
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py` — `TestChangedFileToGroup` tests

## Dependencies

- None — this is the foundational change that other children depend on.

## Goal

Update `changed_scope_selection` to iterate all matched groups (from the new multi-group `select_group_from_changed_files`), union their commands, and check outside-group files against the union of all matched groups\’s `paths`.

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection` currently calls `select_group_from_changed_files` which returns a single group, then computes outside-group files only relative to that one group. When multiple groups match, only the first groupsquo;s outside files are checked, and the otherssquo; test files are silently dropped.

## Requirements

- `ChangedScopeSelection.group` changes from `str | None` to `frozenset[str] | None`.
- `changed_scope_selection` iterates all groups in the frozenset and unions their commands.
- `_changed_outside_group_paths` is updated (or a multi-group variant added) to check changed files outside the **union** of all matched groups\’s `paths`.
- Fail-closed rule preserved: if a changed file outside all matched groups has no selectable file-level command → `commands is None` with `CHANGED_SCOPE_GROUP_INCOMPLETE`.
- A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands via `_union_commands`).

## Impact

A cross-skill change set that touches multiple groups now runs all affected suites in the changed-scope gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A change touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**`, `skill/audit/**` invokes all three groups\’s suite commands.
- AC2: A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands).
- AC3: No group match → existing fallback behaviour unchanged (file-level selection, then full).

## Goal

Implement the deterministic time-attribution metrics engine in `skill/shared/session_time_metrics.py` consumed by the session-time-analysis CLI and agent-log-review alike: union (de-duplicated) and naive-sum active wall-clock, LLM vs tool split, per-tool time/calls/errors, per-model time, token & cache economics, blocking classification by primary binary/first token, hung-command outlier flagging, top-N longest commands, and timezone-correct day windowing (parent AC2–AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria
